text:
ravi: heads-up: eu-west1c started a churn spiral ~10m ago, lots of tiny inference jobs bouncing and eviction rate spiked
emma: saw it on the dashboard, eviction_rate jumped to ~7/min for ~8 minutes
ops-oncall: quick probe shows two cohorts of nodes: some have label `gpu-health=ok` others `gpu-health=soft-fail` after a kernel module upgrade rollback
sundar: what failed exactly?
ops-oncall: nodes that rolled kernel package `nvidia-dkms=470.84` fell back to older driver during boot because the dkms build failed (missing headers). kubelet added `gpu-health=soft-fail` to those nodes via the node-health controller
ravi: scheduler treats `gpu-health=soft-fail` as acceptable for single-slot tiny jobs, but when a gang (multi-pod job) needs all-gpu-topology we later evict the tiny jobs to consolidate, causing repack loops
emma: timeline shows a CI rollout from deploy-bot right before the scale event
deploy-bot: rolling update gpu-node-image v2026-03-23-rc1 at 6812349800
ops-oncall: autoscaler spun up new nodes during a brief image-mirror DNS timeout; some nodes booted from fallback AMI that didn't have the kernel headers preinstalled -> dkms build fails -> label drift
sundar: so two failure modes: fallback AMI + dkms build fail -> label soft-fail. Then descheduler/desire to compact causes eviction of tiny pods. Amplifying loop
ravi: mitigation plan (short): cordon all `gpu-health=soft-fail` nodes in eu-west1c, move tiny jobs to warmpool, reprovision image with headers baked in
emma: I'll cordon+drain the worst offenders now: `kubectl get nodes -l region=eu-west1c,gpu-health=soft-fail -o name | xargs -n1 kubectl cordon`
ops-oncall: running a quick check command:
```
kubectl get nodes -l region=eu-west1c -o custom-columns=NODE:.metadata.name,AMI:.spec.providerID,HEALTH:.metadata.labels.gpu-health --no-headers
```
ops-oncall: sample output:
```
node-12a  gce://redwood-eu/gpu-ami-fallback    soft-fail
node-14b  gce://redwood-eu/gpu-ami-standard    ok
node-15c  gce://redwood-eu/gpu-ami-fallback    soft-fail
node-16d  gce://redwood-eu/gpu-ami-standard    ok
```
sundar: longer term: pin autoscaler to AMI ids (no more ambiguous tags for scale-up), and bake kernel headers in the AMI image to avoid dkms at boot, or run a post-boot init job with retry/backoff that marks node ready once dkms succeeds
ravi: scheduler tweaks: add a soft preference that avoids placing short-lived (<90s) pods on nodes marked `gpu-health=soft-fail`, and change compaction to wait X seconds (120s) before evicting micro-jobs
emma: also recommend pausing the descheduler canary in eu-west1c while we clean up; it's doing opportunistic pack compaction and nudging evictions right now
ops-oncall: descheduler canary paused for 30m in eu-west1c
cost-team-bot: notice: eviction churn increased billed GPU-hours by ~2.4 node-hours in the last 10m in eu-west1c
sundar: we should also add an alert that fires when: `count(node_label_mismatch{label="gpu-health"}) > 3 AND sum(rate(kube_pod_evictions_total[5m])) by (region) > 3`
ravi: filing ticket INF-4621 with repro steps, node list, and `journalctl` failures attached. assigning to infra-image and node-health teams
emma: reprovision run queued: will bake images with headers + DKMS smoke check, then roll nodes back into pool in small batches
ops-oncall: cordon/drain in progress on 2 nodes; ~11 pods being rescheduled, ETA ~5m
sundar: will open PR for scheduler soft-preference and compaction grace window; will include an e2e that simulates dkms fallback nodes so we don't regress
ravi: thanks all — keeping thread live until nodes are back to `gpu-health=ok` :thumbsup:
